title: Unit 8 test: Applications of Integration
author: bc-tests-extensions
directions: Original Liminal practice. Section I Part A and Section II Part B are without a calculator; the other parts require a graphing calculator. Show supporting work and justify conclusions in free response. Angles are in radians. Use exact answers without a calculator and three decimal places for calculator work unless a question specifies otherwise. Report raw practice points only.

figures.alt: The graph of f is made of segments joining (0, 0), (2, 4), and (4, 0).

parts.title: No calculator
parts.directions: Select one answer for each question.

items.prompt: What is the average value of the displayed function f on [0, 4]?
items.rationale: The triangular area is (1/2)(4)(4) = 8. Dividing by the interval length 4 gives an average value of 2.

distractorNotes.B: This is the maximum function value, not the average.
distractorNotes.C: This is the area under the graph without division by interval length.
distractorNotes.D: This divides the triangular area by twice the interval length.

items.prompt: A particle has velocity v(t) = t^2 − 4 for 0 ≤ t ≤ 3. Which pair gives its displacement and total distance traveled over that interval?
items.rationale: An antiderivative is t^3/3 − 4t, giving displacement −3. Velocity changes sign at t = 2, giving distance 16/3 + 7/3 = 23/3.

distractorNotes.A: This takes the absolute value after integrating instead of integrating absolute velocity.
distractorNotes.B: This treats backward travel as positive displacement.
distractorNotes.D: This reverses the sign of the net displacement.

items.prompt: What is the total area between y = x and y = x^3 on −1 ≤ x ≤ 1?
items.rationale: The curves meet at −1, 0, and 1. The upper curve switches at 0. Symmetry gives 2∫ from 0 to 1 of (x − x^3) dx = 1/2.

distractorNotes.A: This computes a signed difference and cancels the two regions.
distractorNotes.B: This includes only the region on [0, 1].
distractorNotes.C: This doubles the total area after symmetry is already included.

items.prompt: The region bounded by x = y^2 and x = 2y lies between y = 0 and y = 2. What is its area?
items.rationale: For 0 ≤ y ≤ 2, 2y ≥ y^2. The area is ∫ from 0 to 2 of (2y − y^2) dy = 4/3.

distractorNotes.A: This integrates y^2 alone instead of right minus left.
distractorNotes.C: This subtracts the right boundary from the left boundary.
distractorNotes.D: This uses the area of a bounding rectangle.

items.prompt: A solid has base bounded by y = 2 − x, y = 0, and x = 0. Cross sections perpendicular to the x-axis are squares whose sides lie in the base. What is the volume?
items.rationale: A cross section at x has side 2 − x and area (2 − x)^2. The volume is ∫ from 0 to 2 of (2 − x)^2 dx = 8/3.

distractorNotes.A: This computes base area instead of volume.
distractorNotes.C: This uses triangular rather than square cross sections.
distractorNotes.D: This uses the largest square area for the whole length.

items.prompt: The region under y = √(1 + x^2), above the x-axis, and between x = 0 and x = 1 is revolved about the x-axis. What is the volume?
items.rationale: Each disc has area π(1 + x^2), so the volume is π∫ from 0 to 1 of (1 + x^2) dx = 4π/3.

distractorNotes.B: This omits the constant 1 from the squared radius.
distractorNotes.D: This omits the factor π in the disc area.

items.prompt: The region between y = x and y = x^2 for 0 ≤ x ≤ 1 is revolved about y = −1. What is the volume?
items.rationale: The outer radius is 1 + x and the inner radius is 1 + x^2. The volume is π∫ from 0 to 1 of (2x − x^2 − x^4) dx = 7π/15.

distractorNotes.A: This revolves the region about the x-axis instead of y = −1.
distractorNotes.B: This squares the difference of the radii instead of subtracting their squares.
distractorNotes.C: This reverses outer and inner radii.

items.prompt: For y = x^3/3 + 1/(4x) on [1, 2], what is the arc length?
items.rationale: Here y′ = x^2 − 1/(4x^2), so 1 + (y′)^2 = [x^2 + 1/(4x^2)]^2. The positive square root integrates to 7/3 + 1/8 = 59/24.

distractorNotes.B: This omits the inverse-square contribution to the length integrand.
distractorNotes.D: This doubles the length after taking the square root.

parts.title: Graphing calculator
parts.directions: Select one answer. Numerical choices are rounded as displayed.

items.prompt: Let a be the positive intersection of y = e^(−x^2) and y = 0.2. What is the area enclosed by these curves and the y-axis?
items.rationale: The intersection is a = √(ln 5). The area is ∫ from 0 to a of [e^(−x^2) − 0.2] dx = 0.567988024.

distractorNotes.A: This integrates the upper curve without subtracting 0.2.
distractorNotes.B: This includes the mirror-image region on the negative x-axis.
distractorNotes.C: This integrates e^(−x^2) from 0 to 2 instead of using the enclosed region.

items.prompt: A hollow casting is filled to form a solid whose circular cross section at x meters has radius 1 + 0.2 sin(x^2) meters, for 0 ≤ x ≤ 3. What is its volume?
items.rationale: The radius remains positive. Integrate π[1 + 0.2 sin(x^2)]^2 from 0 to 3 to obtain 10.561537484 m^3.

distractorNotes.A: This replaces the varying radius by 1 throughout.
distractorNotes.C: This omits π from the circular cross-sectional area.
distractorNotes.D: This uses a half-disc instead of the full circular cross section.

items.prompt: A wire follows y = sin(x^2) for 0 ≤ x ≤ 1, with both coordinates in meters. What is its length?
items.rationale: The derivative is 2x cos(x^2). The length is ∫ from 0 to 1 of √[1 + 4x^2 cos^2(x^2)] dx = 1.349235229 m.

distractorNotes.A: This is the change in height, not the arc length.
distractorNotes.B: This is the horizontal span, not the arc length.
distractorNotes.D: This uses an incorrect derivative in the length integrand.

items.prompt: A moving slider has velocity v(t) = sin(t^2) + 0.3t meters per second for 0 ≤ t ≤ 3. What is its average velocity on this interval?
items.rationale: Average velocity is (1/3)∫ from 0 to 3 of [sin(t^2) + 0.3t] dt = 0.707854176 m/s.

distractorNotes.B: This is displacement without division by elapsed time.
distractorNotes.D: This uses the final velocity instead of its average.

parts.title: Graphing calculator
parts.directions: Show integral or equation setups and justify conclusions.

items.prompt: A robot moves along a straight rail. Its position x(t) is in meters, x(0) = 2, and its signed velocity is v(t) = cos(t^2/3) − 0.25t for 0 ≤ t ≤ 4 seconds. Positive velocity means motion to the right.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find every time in (0, 4) when the robot changes direction. Explain how you determined that each time gives a direction change.
parts.answer: t = 1.816 s, changing from rightward to leftward.
steps: The velocity is positive before this root and negative after it. For t ≥ 2, cos(t^2/3) cannot meet 0.25t: on [2, √(3π)] it is at most cos(4/3) < 0.5, and on [√(3π), 4] it is at most cos(16/3) < 0.6 < 0.25√(3π).
On [0, 2], v′ = −(2t/3)sin(t^2/3) − 0.25 < 0, so only one root occurs there.

rubric.criterion: Provides evidence that velocity changes sign from positive to negative.
Establishes no other direction changes on the interval, by a complete graph/sign analysis or equivalent reasoning.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the robot’s position at t = 4, with units.
steps: Use x(4) = 2 + ∫ from 0 to 4 of v(t) dt.
The displacement is −1.231608238 m, giving x(4) = 0.768391762 m.

rubric.criterion: Sets up initial position plus signed velocity integral.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the total distance traveled on [0, 4], with units.
steps: The distance is ∫ from 0 to 4 of |v(t)| dt.
Equivalently split at r = 1.816175304 and subtract the integral on [r, 4] from that on [0, r].

rubric.criterion: Uses absolute velocity or a correct sign-based split.
Evaluates with the correct reversal time.

items.prompt: Let R be the bounded region between y = 2x and y = x^2. All lengths below are measured in meters.

parts.label: a
steps: Intersections satisfy x^2 = 2x, so x = 0 and x = 2.
On [0, 2], 2x is the upper curve; area = ∫ from 0 to 2 of (2x − x^2) dx = 4/3.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A solid has base R and equilateral-triangle cross sections perpendicular to the x-axis. Each triangle has one side in R. Find the volume. The area of an equilateral triangle of side s is √3 s^2/4.
steps: The triangle side is 2x − x^2, so its area is (√3/4)(2x − x^2)^2.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the side as the vertical width 2x − x^2.
Uses the triangular cross-sectional area in a volume integral.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the volume formed when R is revolved about the line y = 5.
steps: The axis lies above R. The outer radius is 5 − x^2 and the inner radius is 5 − 2x.
Volume = π∫ from 0 to 2 of [(5 − x^2)^2 − (5 − 2x)^2] dx.
The integrand is π(20x − 14x^2 + x^4), yielding 136π/15.
Alternatively, horizontal cylindrical shells give 2π∫ from 0 to 4 of (5 − y)(√y − y/2) dy, with the same volume.

rubric.criterion: Identifies correct washer radii or horizontal-shell radius and height relative to y = 5.
Sets up a correct volume integral with matching bounds for the chosen method.
